title: What breaks a good mix
objectives: Name the six behaviours that break a well-built allocation.
Give the compliant response to each.
body_md:
A well-built allocation fails only when the client abandons it.

| Behaviour | What it sounds like | What to say |
|---|---|---|
| Chasing last year's winner | "Gold did 20% last year; move everything there." | "Each asset has its year. The mix is built so we don't have to guess which one is next." |
| Debt feels like a drag | "Why keep debt earning 7% when equity did 25%?" | "Debt is the part that lets you sleep in a bad year, and it's what we buy equity with after a fall." |
| All in FDs | "I don't want any risk." | "FDs carry inflation risk. Let's look at what ₹10 L in FDs buys in 15 years versus a balanced mix." |
| Concentration | "Most of my money is in my company's shares." | "Let's count it in your mix and diversify the new money around it." |
| Mental accounting | "My EPF and PPF are separate; they don't count." | "They're debt. Counting them may mean your mutual funds can hold more equity." |
| Rebalancing feels wrong | "Why sell equity when it's doing well?" | "We're taking some profit to get back to your agreed mix, not predicting a fall." |

**The one line to remember:** the best mix is the one the client can stick with through a bad year.
example: After a strong year for gold, Vikram wants to move his whole portfolio into gold. The answer keeps gold at the agreed 10% and explains that each asset has its year, without predicting the next one.
say: Each asset has its year, and the mix means we don't have to guess which is next.
We're returning to your agreed mix, not predicting a fall.
never: Gold is the place to be now.
Debt is a waste of money in a bull market.

check.q: A client wants to move most of the portfolio into gold after a strong year. What is the right response?
o: Each asset has its year; keep gold to the agreed share, often 5–15%
Move everything to gold and review in a year
check.why: The mix exists so nobody has to guess which asset is next. Gold stays at its agreed share.

check.q: A client says debt is a drag at 7% while equity did 25%. Best answer?
o: Sell the debt and buy equity
Debt is what lets you sleep in a bad year, and what we buy equity with after a fall
Debt is pointless at your age
Let's move to a sectoral fund
check.why: Debt is the ballast, and the dry powder for the next fall.

check.q: A client's wealth is mostly in his employer's shares. What should happen?
o: Ignore it; we don't manage it
Count it in the mix and diversify new money around it
Move the mutual funds to the same sector
check.why: Concentration belongs in the picture: count it, then diversify new money around it.
